title: Australian Citizenship Photo Requirements (Online and Paper)
metaTitle: Australian Citizenship Photo Requirements: Size and Upload
metaDescription: Australian citizenship photo rules: under 6 months old, light grey or neutral background, JPEG 70 KB to 3.5 MB online, 35-40 x 45-50 mm on paper.
excerpt: What photo you need for an Australian citizenship application, online or on paper: file type, file size, print size, head size and the pose rules Home Affairs sets.
keyTakeaways: The photo must be no more than 6 months old.
Use a neutral or light grey background that contrasts with your face.
Online: a JPEG file between 70 KB and 3.5 MB, preferably 1200 x 1600 pixels.
Paper: 35-40 mm wide x 45-50 mm high, with 32-36 mm from chin to crown.
No editing at all, and no scans of photos or photos of photos.
intro: **Quick answer:** Your Australian citizenship photo must be no more than 6 months old, on a neutral or light grey background, with no editing. For an online application, upload a JPEG between 70 KB and 3.5 MB (1200 x 1600 pixels is preferred). For a paper application, the photo is 35-40 mm wide x 45-50 mm high, with your head 32-36 mm from chin to crown.

> **Important:** The Department of Home Affairs recommends a professional photo provider and does not recommend online photo services or apps for citizenship photos. Use our tool to check or prepare a photo, but always confirm it meets the official guidelines before you apply.
**[Check my photo with the Australian passport photo checker →](/australian-passport-photo-checker)**

This guide covers the citizenship photo only. If you are applying for a passport after your ceremony, the passport has its own print rules, covered in our [Australian passport photo requirements](/guides/australian-passport-photo-requirements) guide.

sections.heading: What photo do you need for an Australian citizenship application?

subsections.heading: Who needs to provide a photo
content: Your application tells you which people in it need a photo. Read the instructions in your online account or on the paper form, and provide a photo for each person it asks for.
Each photo must follow the same rules, including photos of children and babies.

subsections.heading: Online vs paper applications
content: The rules for how you look in the photo are the same either way. What changes is the format.

| Application type | What you provide |
|---|---|
| Online | A digital JPEG file, 70 KB to 3.5 MB, preferred 1200 x 1600 pixels |
| Paper | A printed photo, 35-40 mm wide x 45-50 mm high, head 32-36 mm chin to crown |
Both must be no more than 6 months old.

subsections.heading: Why Home Affairs recommends a professional provider
content: Home Affairs recommends a professional photo provider and names Australia Post as its recommended option. It does not recommend online photo services or apps.
A professional provider knows the lighting, background and framing rules, and can usually take a new photo on the spot if the first one is not right.

sections.heading: What are the photo quality and pose rules?

subsections.heading: Neutral or light grey background that contrasts with your face
content: Stand in front of a plain neutral or light grey background. It needs to contrast with your face so the edges of your head are easy to see.
Avoid patterned walls, doors, shelves or anything else behind you.

subsections.heading: Face centred, eyes open, mouth closed, neutral expression
content: Look straight at the camera with your face centred in the frame. Keep your eyes open, your mouth closed and your expression neutral.
Keep your hair off your face so your features are clear.

subsections.heading: No editing (no background removal, no retouching)
content: Home Affairs does not accept edited photos. That means:

- no background removal or replacement
- no removing moles, wrinkles or scars
- no red-eye removal
- no filters or beauty modes
If your photo has a problem, take a new one instead of fixing it in an app.

sections.heading: What are the online upload requirements?

subsections.heading: JPEG, 70 KB to 3.5 MB
content: Save the photo as a JPEG file. The file must be at least 70 KB and no more than 3.5 MB.
Messaging apps and email often shrink photos without telling you. Check the file size on your computer or phone before you upload.

subsections.heading: Preferred resolution 1200 x 1600 pixels
content: Home Affairs prefers a resolution of 1200 x 1600 pixels (width x height). That is a portrait photo with a 3:4 shape.
Ask your photo provider for a digital copy at this size, or check the file details before you upload.

subsections.heading: Why a scan or a photo of a photo is not accepted
content: Home Affairs does not accept a scan of a printed photo or a photo taken of a printed photo. Copies lose detail and can pick up glare, lines and colour changes.
Use the original digital file from the camera or provider.

sections.heading: What are the paper application requirements?

subsections.heading: Size 35-40 mm wide x 45-50 mm high
content: A printed citizenship photo must be 35-40 mm wide and 45-50 mm high. A 35 x 45 mm photo sits inside this range.
For the size in cm and inches, see our [Australian passport photo size](/guides/australian-passport-photo-size) guide, which uses the same measurements.

subsections.heading: Head size 32-36 mm
content: Measure from the bottom of your chin to the top of your head (the crown). It must be 32-36 mm on the print.
This is the measurement people most often get wrong when they reuse a photo made for another country.

subsections.heading: How recent the photo must be (no more than 6 months)
content: Your photo must be no more than 6 months old when you apply. An older photo is not acceptable, even if you look the same.
If your application takes a while to prepare, check the date the photo was taken before you lodge it.

sections.heading: Can you wear glasses, head coverings or jewellery?

subsections.heading: Glasses must be removed (medical exceptions)
content: Take your glasses off for the photo. If you must wear them for medical reasons, the lenses must be untinted, the frames must not cross your eyes, and there must be no reflection on the lenses.

subsections.heading: Religious head coverings (plain, whole face visible)
content: Home Affairs lists hair off the face and a centred, straight-on face as pose rules. If you wear a head covering for religious reasons, make sure your whole face is clearly visible.
The Passport Office also asks for plain head coverings with no patterns. Following that rule is a sensible choice for your citizenship photo too.

subsections.heading: Jewellery and reflections
content: Make sure nothing covers your face or reflects light into the camera. Shiny jewellery near the face can create glare.
If in doubt, remove it for the photo.

sections.heading: What are the rules for babies and children?

subsections.heading: Infants under 3 (open mouth acceptable)
content: For a child under 3, an open mouth is acceptable. The other rules still apply: plain background, face straight on and no editing.
For tips on photographing a baby, see our [baby passport photo guide](/guides/australian-baby-passport-photo).

subsections.heading: No other person or object in the photo
content: No other person or object can be visible. That includes a parent's hands, toys and dummies.
A good provider can help you position a baby without anyone appearing in the frame.

sections.heading: How do you get a citizenship photo?

subsections.heading: Using a professional provider (Australia Post is recommended)
content: Home Affairs recommends a professional provider, and names Australia Post. Tell them the photo is for an Australian citizenship application so they use the right rules.
See [where to get an Australian passport photo](/guides/where-to-get-australian-passport-photo) for the types of providers you can use.

subsections.heading: Getting a digital copy for an online application
content: If you are applying online, ask the provider whether they can give you a digital file as well as prints. Check that it is a JPEG between 70 KB and 3.5 MB before you upload it.
Do not photograph or scan the prints instead. That is not accepted.

subsections.heading: Checking it before you upload (tool CTA)
content: Our [Australian passport photo checker](/australian-passport-photo-checker) is a quick pre-check. It looks at head height, background, lighting and glasses, and tells you what to fix.
It is a check only. A pass does not mean Home Affairs will accept the photo, so always compare it with the official guidelines as well.

subsections.heading: Department of Home Affairs
content: - [Photo requirements for citizenship applications](https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/citizenship/apply-for-citizenship/prepare-application/photo-requirements) (page updated 7 October 2026)

subsections.heading: Australian Passport Office
content: - [Passport photo guidelines](https://www.passports.gov.au/PhotoGuidelines), for the passport you may apply for after your ceremony

subsections.heading: Last updated
content: Last updated: 21 November 2026. We checked these rules against the official pages on this date.
Rules and file limits change, so we review this page every 3 months. Always read the official page on the day you apply.

faq.question: What size is an Australian citizenship photo?
faq.answer: For a paper application, the photo is 35-40 mm wide x 45-50 mm high, with your head 32-36 mm from chin to crown. For an online application, upload a JPEG between 70 KB and 3.5 MB. Home Affairs prefers a resolution of 1200 x 1600 pixels for online photos.

faq.question: Can I take my own citizenship photo?
faq.answer: Home Affairs recommends a professional provider, such as Australia Post, and does not recommend online photo services or apps. If you take your own, it must still meet every rule, with no editing at all. Our checker can help you spot problems, but it cannot promise acceptance.

faq.question: Can I wear glasses in my citizenship photo?
faq.answer: No, you should remove them. If you need glasses for medical reasons, the lenses must be untinted, the frames must not cover your eyes, and there must be no reflection on the lenses. Taking glasses off avoids glare and frame problems completely.

faq.question: How old can my citizenship photo be?
faq.answer: The photo must be no more than 6 months old. This applies to both online and paper applications. If you took the photo for an earlier application, check the date before you reuse it, and take a new one if more than 6 months have passed.

faq.question: What file type can I upload for an online citizenship application?
faq.answer: Upload a JPEG file between 70 KB and 3.5 MB. Home Affairs prefers 1200 x 1600 pixels. Use the original digital file, because a scan of a printed photo or a photo of a photo is not accepted. Check the file size before you start the upload.

cta.title: Pre-check your citizenship photo
cta.text: Upload your photo to check head height, background, lighting and glasses before you apply. A pass is a guide, not an approval.
